spec.title: Surfaces rest on observed landmarks
spec.input: every surface extraction over the live landmark map
spec.expected: surfaces whose every landmark is in the map they were extracted from, and none before a landmark was confirmed
spec.passCriteria: >= 8 extractions; at least one surface of >= 20 landmarks; 0 surfaces naming a landmark the map did not hold; 0 surfaces from a map with no confirmed landmark
spec.failureCondition: a surface with no landmarks under it, or one that appeared before the map had anything confirmed (Rule 002)

testResults.observed: 3 surface(s) over 288 of 300 confirmed landmarks after 13 extractions: {"WALL":1,"GROUND":1,"UNKNOWN":1}
testResults.reason: every surface rests on landmarks the map holds, and none appeared before the map had any

spec.title: Planar
spec.input: the RMS distance of each surface’s landmarks from its plane, relative to the scene depth
spec.expected: landmarks that lie on their plane far inside the inlier band
spec.passCriteria: median residual <= 0.015 of a depth (half the 0.03 band)
spec.failureCondition: a median residual that fills the band — the signature of a slice through a cloud, not a surface

testResults.reason: the landmarks lie on their planes well inside the band — uniform filling would put the median near 0.58 of it

spec.title: Persistent
spec.input: each extraction’s surfaces against the previous extraction’s
spec.expected: the same surfaces found again as the map grows, under the same ids
spec.passCriteria: >= 8 surfaces offered for re-finding; >= 70% found again
spec.failureCondition: surfaces that do not survive the next extraction — a detector reporting its own noise

testResults.reason: surfaces persist across extractions, as observed structure does and noise does not

spec.title: Nothing from structureless points
spec.input: the same landmarks, each moved ten inlier bands in a seeded direction, through the same extraction
spec.expected: the control’s largest surface far smaller than the room’s
spec.passCriteria: >= 3 control runs; median ratio of largest-surface support <= 0.3
spec.failureCondition: a control that yields surfaces rivalling the real ones — the thresholds are finding planes in anything

testResults.observed: control's largest surface is 16.6% of the room's (worst 19.5%) over 3 runs
testResults.reason: jittering the landmarks off their planes removes the surfaces — they were in the landmarks, not in the thresholds

spec.title: Classified only against measured gravity
spec.input: every classified surface, and the gravity state it was classified under
spec.expected: no GROUND, WALL, PLATFORM or OBSTACLE while gravity is UNKNOWN; every class consistent with its tilt
spec.failureCondition: a floor named before anything measured down (v4 §1.4 PLANE: UNKNOWN)

testResults.reason: nothing was called a floor or a wall before down was measured

spec.title: Down, measured
spec.input: localized frames paired with the orientation sensor’s down vector
spec.expected: one image layout under which every frame agrees on down, clearly better than the others
spec.passCriteria: >= 30 pairings over >= 15° of viewing direction; best spread <= 6°; runner-up at least twice as spread and 2° worse
spec.failureCondition: a down vector assumed, or chosen from data that could not tell the layouts apart

testResults.observed: down agreed to 0.336° under the 0° layout (runner-up 5.398°) over 75 frames spanning 31.06°
testResults.reason: the pose and the orientation sensor agree on one down direction, and the motion separated the layouts

spec.title: A ground to play on
spec.passCriteria: at least one GROUND surface at that confidence, with the camera height above it measured
spec.failureCondition: none — and the game cannot start, which is the correct outcome rather than a fake floor

testResults.observed: 1 GROUND surface(s), best confidence 0.5848; camera 8.080237 units above it
testResults.reason: an observed floor, measured against gravity

spec.title: Extraction cost
spec.input: wall time of each extraction on the main thread
spec.expected: small enough to run beside the render loop about once a second

spec.title: The accelerometer agrees with the orientation sensor
spec.input: `accelerationIncludingGravity` near 1 g, against the orientation-derived down, with its sign measured
spec.expected: agreement within a few degrees, and the sign recorded rather than assumed
spec.failureCondition: two gravity sensors on one phone disagreeing about down

testResults.reason: the two sensors agree, and the sign convention was measured on this device

controller.note: Every decision carries the median worker latency and the budget it was compared against. The controller reads no clock of its own — only the timestamps on the samples it is given (§59).

segmentLog.note: The timeline is cut wherever load injection was switched on or off. FRAME-001 reads the longest unstressed segment; stressed segments are measured and reported but never counted toward continuity.

crossCheckDetail.note: Each pair is one video frame measured twice: on the main thread with an independent 64x48 readback, and in the worker on the pixels the pipeline actually delivered. The readback costs what §H.1 measured, which is why it runs at 1 Hz and is excluded from the pipeline UI cost in FRAME-005.

pipeline.note: Frames declined by rate pacing (pacedOut) are the scheduler working as designed and are not drops. Frames declined because the worker was busy (backpressured) are deliberate too. Only `lost` counts frames that were handed over and never came back, and only that is held against FRAME-001.
